summary: Hawaii currently has NO lawful import pathway for a pet roof rat, confirmed in writing by the Hawaii Department of Agriculture and Biosecurity (2026-06-15). Hawaii regulates animal imports through lists under HAR Chapter 4-71. The Conditionally Approved list does include a Family Muridae entry for Rattus sp. (rat, domesticated), but the Department clarified that the permit conditions the Board has actually established for that entry apply specifically to the Norway rat (Rattus norvegicus); there are no established permit conditions authorizing the importation of Rattus rattus for private pet ownership. And because Rattus sp. is already on the Conditionally Approved list, R. rattus is NOT treated as an unlisted animal, so the case-by-case special permit under HRS 150A-6.2(c) (which applies only to unlisted animals) is not available either. The Branch therefore cannot issue an import permit for a pet R. rattus. The only route is to petition the Board of Agriculture and Biosecurity to establish permit conditions for the species, which the Department says takes about one to two years, runs through advisory committees, and is not guaranteed. So keeping, breeding, selling, and importing a pet roof rat are all effectively prohibited in Hawaii today (the bar is the import gate), with a multi-year regulatory petition as the only pathway. This is a species trap: the fancy rat (R. norvegicus) has established import conditions and the roof rat does not. Wild and feral R. rattus is separately a major invasive pest and disease vector in Hawaii; never release one.
agency_confirmations: The Hawaii Department of Agriculture and Biosecurity (its Land Vertebrate Specialist, Plant Quarantine Branch) confirmed in writing on 15 June 2026 that the Conditionally Approved Rattus sp. (rat, domesticated) entry's permit conditions apply specifically to Rattus norvegicus, and that the Branch has no established permit conditions authorizing the importation of Rattus rattus for private pet ownership.

Because Rattus sp. is already on the Conditionally Approved list, Rattus rattus is not an unlisted animal, so the case-by-case special permit under HRS 150A-6.2(c) is not available for it. The Branch cannot issue an import permit for a pet roof rat.

The only route is to ask the Board of Agriculture and Biosecurity to establish permit conditions for domesticated Rattus rattus. The Department said this process takes about one to two years, is evaluated by advisory committees of subject-matter experts, and is not guaranteed to be approved.

The Department further detailed the full process (June 2026) to establish import permit conditions for a Conditionally Approved animal: submit Form PQ-7 plus a completed Board Submittal Template (request the current template from the Plant Quarantine Branch) with supporting documents; the request is then reviewed by the Advisory Subcommittee on Land Vertebrates (biosecurity, containment, and risk-management), undergoes legal review by a Deputy Attorney General, is heard at a public Advisory Committee for Plants and Animals meeting, goes through draft minutes and any revisions, and is finally presented to the Board of Agriculture and Biosecurity at a public meeting, which may approve, deny, or defer it.

kit.problem: In Hawaii, keeping a pet roof rat (Rattus rattus) currently has no lawful pathway, while the closely related fancy rat (the Norway rat, Rattus norvegicus) can be imported and kept under established permit conditions. Hawaii's Conditionally Approved Animals list (HAR 4-71) includes a genus-level entry for Rattus sp. (rat, domesticated), but the Department of Agriculture and Biosecurity has confirmed in writing that the permit conditions the Board actually established for that entry apply specifically to the Norway rat, and that there are no established permit conditions for importing the roof rat as a pet. Because Rattus sp. is already listed, the roof rat is not an unlisted animal, so the usual case-by-case special permit is unavailable too. The result is a species trap created by which rat the conditions were written for: two domesticated, captive-bred, indoor pet rats of nearly identical risk are treated oppositely, one importable, one not.
kit.ask: Ask the Hawaii Department of Agriculture and Biosecurity to begin the process of establishing import permit conditions for the domesticated, captive-bred roof rat (Rattus rattus), so it is treated like the already-permitted Norway rat (Rattus norvegicus). The Department itself identified this as the route: a request to the Board of Agriculture and Biosecurity, evaluated by its advisory committees, to set permit conditions for the species (the Department offered to explain how to begin). The relevant question is domestication, not wild ancestry: the dog descends from the wolf and the house cat from a wild felid, yet both are recognized as domestic animals because of generations bred for tameness. The Norway rat that already has conditions is itself the wild brown rat, domesticated in the 19th century, so a captive-bred roof rat is the same case one species over (https://blonderoofrat.com/how-the-sewer-rat-became-the-fancy-rat/). This is a long process (the Department says about one to two years and approval is not guaranteed), so it suits a committed keeper or an organized group; the ask is that the Board weigh establishing conditions, not that it reach a particular result.
kit.branch_note:
Lever = the agency, specifically the Board of Agriculture and Biosecurity acting through the Plant Quarantine Branch, not the legislature. No statute bans the roof rat; HRS 150A directs the Board to maintain the lists and set import permit conditions, and the Department has confirmed the missing piece is Board-established permit conditions for R. rattus. The fix is therefore a Board submittal to add those conditions (the Department offered to explain how to begin), reinforced through the advisory-committee review the Department described. Going to the legislature would be the wrong door; there is no anti-rat statute to repeal. The case-by-case special permit is NOT a usable lever here, because the Department confirmed it applies only to unlisted animals and R. rattus is already listed at the genus level.

The process (agency-described, June 2026): (1) submit Form PQ-7 + a Board Submittal Template (request the current template from dab.pqlvs@hawaii.gov) with supporting documents; (2) Advisory Subcommittee on Land Vertebrates review (allow at least two weeks); (3) legal review by a Deputy Attorney General; (4) a public Advisory Committee for Plants and Animals meeting (recommendation); (5) draft minutes + any requested revisions; (6) a Board of Agriculture and Biosecurity public meeting for the final decision (approve, deny, or defer). It is a multi-step, expert-and-legal-reviewed petition (the Department earlier estimated roughly one to two years with no guaranteed outcome), but it is the real, agency-named pathway, the same kind of permit-condition process the Norway rat already cleared.

template.en:
To: Hawaii Department of Agriculture & Biosecurity, Plant Quarantine Branch

Re: Establishing import permit conditions for the domesticated roof rat (Rattus rattus)

I understand from the Department that the Conditionally Approved entry for Rattus sp. (rat, domesticated) currently carries permit conditions established only for the Norway rat (Rattus norvegicus), and that there are no permit conditions authorizing the importation of the domesticated roof rat (Rattus rattus) as a pet, so the Branch cannot currently issue a permit for one. I would like to begin the process of asking the Board of Agriculture and Biosecurity to establish permit conditions for domesticated, captive-bred Rattus rattus, so it can be kept under the same kind of conditions as the Norway rat.

The animals in question are multi-generation, captive-bred, hand-tame roof rats kept strictly indoors in secure enclosures and never released. What makes an animal domestic is its breeding history, not its wild ancestry: the dog descends from the wolf and the house cat from a wild felid, yet both are recognized as domestic animals. The Norway rat that already has conditions is itself the wild brown rat, domesticated in the 19th century, so a captive-bred roof rat is the same case one species over.

Could you please tell me how to begin this request, what information the Board and its advisory committees would need, and the expected timeline? I understand approval is not guaranteed and the review takes time, and I am prepared to provide whatever husbandry, containment, and provenance information would help the Board weigh it.

Thank you for your time and help.

[Your name]
[Your city, Hawaii]
[Your email / phone]

kit.confidence_notes: Verified 2026-06-13 against Hawaii primary sources. RESOLVED (key correction vs the preliminary JSON): the current Conditionally Approved list (HAR §4-71-6.5, Exhibit AR-71C) was text-extracted from the official HDOA PDF and reads verbatim, under FAMILY Muridae: 'Mus musculus mice, domesticated' and 'Rattus sp. rat, domesticated.' The rats entry is GENUS-LEVEL ('Rattus sp.'), NOT species-specific to R. norvegicus, so on the face of the rule a domesticated R. rattus is within the entry. CONFIRMED: (a) HAR §4-71-6.5 (Cornell LII) references the conditionally-approved list 'located at the end of this chapter' and imports conditionally-approved animals by permit; (b) the Prohibited list (AR-71P, §4-71-6) was text-extracted and contains Family Cricetidae, Erethizontidae, Hystricidae, and Sciuridae under Order Rodentia but NO Family Muridae and NO Rattus or Mus - R. rattus is not prohibited; (c) HRS §150A-6.2 (Justia) directs the Board to maintain the lists, import conditionally-approved/restricted animals by permit, prohibit unlisted animals until Board review, and issue case-by-case special permits (incl. a 90-day short-term special permit); (d) 50 CFR 14.4 (Cornell LII) defines 'domesticated animals' and names 'White lab mouse - Mus musculus' and 'White lab rat - Rattus norvegicus' but NOT Rattus rattus, so for INTERNATIONAL movement (not mainland-to-Hawaii) USFWS treats R. rattus as wildlife. RESIDUAL UNCERTAINTY (now interpretive, not textual): HDOA's permit submittals (e.g., the May 2023 / UH Animal & Veterinary Services PQ-7 packets) describe the imported 'domesticated rat' as R. norvegicus and justify approval by its 'degree of domestication,' and the Chief Plant Inspector exercises species discretion at permit time - so whether HDOA will read the genus entry to cover a captive-bred R. rattus, and what conditions/fee/processing time apply to a private pet permit, should be confirmed directly with the Branch. The permit fee schedule ($20 single-shipment / $100 unlimited / $250 expedited per HAR §4-71-3.1, per the DR) and the 7-day CVI window and Honolulu-only entry (per the HDOA importing-animals guidance, per the DR) were taken from the DR and should be reconfirmed against the current HDOA fee/importing pages before relying on them. No dedicated permit-inquiry email is published, so the official application page and contacts page are used rather than an unverified inbox. This is a research aid, not legal advice; the binding answer is HDOA's written determination. UPDATE 2026-06-15 (RESOLVED by agency, supersedes the genus-text optimism above): HDOA (its Land Vertebrate Specialist) confirmed in writing that the Rattus sp. permit conditions are R. norvegicus-specific, there are no R. rattus permit conditions, and the case-by-case special permit (HRS 150A-6.2(c)) does NOT apply because R. rattus is already listed (not unlisted). So import is currently impossible for a pet roof rat; the only route is a Board petition to establish conditions (about 1-2 years, advisory-committee review, not guaranteed). Verified inbox dab.pqlvs@hawaii.gov; phone (808) 832-0566.

keep.why: No lawful pathway: a pet roof rat cannot be lawfully imported into Hawaii (see transport), and possession of a non-domestic animal without a valid import permit is unlawful under HAR 4-71 / HRS 150A. HDOA confirmed in writing (2026-06-15) that there are no established permit conditions for importing R. rattus and that the case-by-case special permit does not apply (R. rattus is already listed at the genus level), so no permit can currently issue. The Norway rat (R. norvegicus) has permit conditions and can be kept; the roof rat cannot, until the Board establishes conditions for it.
keep.governing_law: HAR 4-71-6.5 (Conditionally Approved list; conditions are R. norvegicus-specific per HDOA); HRS 150A-6.2 (import by permit; case-by-case special permit only for unlisted animals); HDOA written determination 2026-06-15.

breed.why: Effectively prohibited as a consequence of the import bar: there is no lawful way to obtain or hold a pet R. rattus in Hawaii (no permit can issue), so there is no lawful animal to breed. If the Board later establishes R. rattus permit conditions, any breeding would be governed by those conditions.

sell_give.why: Effectively prohibited as a consequence of the import bar: with no lawful pathway to import or possess a pet R. rattus, there is no lawfully held animal to sell or give away within Hawaii.

transport.why: Import of a pet roof rat is currently not permitted. HDOA confirmed in writing (2026-06-15) that the Conditionally Approved Rattus sp. permit conditions apply only to R. norvegicus, that there are no permit conditions for importing R. rattus as a pet, and that the case-by-case special permit (HRS 150A-6.2(c)) is unavailable because R. rattus is already listed (not unlisted). The Branch therefore cannot issue an import permit. The only route is to petition the Board of Agriculture and Biosecurity to establish permit conditions (about 1-2 years, not guaranteed). For any international movement, USFWS separately treats R. rattus as wildlife under 50 CFR 14.4. Never release a roof rat.
transport.governing_law: HAR 4-71-3 / 4-71-6.5; HRS 150A-6.2; HDOA written determination 2026-06-15; 50 CFR 14.4 (international only).

restrictions.summary: There is currently NO lawful way to import or keep a pet roof rat in Hawaii. HDOA confirmed in writing (2026-06-15) that the Conditionally Approved 'Rattus sp.' permit conditions were established for the Norway rat (R. norvegicus) only, that there are no permit conditions for importing R. rattus as a pet, and that the case-by-case special permit does not apply because the genus is already listed, so the Plant Quarantine Branch cannot issue an import permit for one. The only route is to petition the Board of Agriculture and Biosecurity to establish permit conditions for the species (about one to two years, advisory-committee and legal review, not guaranteed, see the Roof Rat Freedoms section below). Never release a roof rat (feral Rattus is an invasive pest).

restrictions.summary: Releasing a pet roof rat into the wild is prohibited and dangerous: feral R. rattus is among the most damaging invasive vertebrates in Hawaii and is separately managed as a public-health vector (DOH HAR 11-26, which bars conditions that harbor or breed rodents). Keep the animal contained at all times and rehome responsibly; never release.
steps: Never release a roof rat into the wild (invasive pest + public-health vector; multiple state violations)

inquiry_focus: (1) Species coverage of the genus entry: the HAR §4-71-6.5 Conditionally Approved list reads 'Rattus sp. - rat, domesticated' (genus-level). Does the Plant Quarantine Branch apply that entry to a domesticated/captive-bred Rattus rattus, so a private resident may obtain a Form PQ-7 permit to keep one as a pet, or does the Branch read it to cover only R. norvegicus? (2) If read narrowly, can a private keeper obtain a case-by-case import permit for a domesticated R. rattus under HRS §150A-6.2, or have the genus entry recognized for R. rattus? (3) For a private keeper importing a few domesticated rats: what standard permit conditions apply, and is there any restriction on breeding or on transferring offspring to other Hawaii residents (do recipients need their own permits)? (4) Current fee and processing time for a Conditionally Approved import permit (Form PQ-7) for domesticated rats.

sources.title: HAR §4-71-6.5 - List of Conditionally Approved Animals (Exhibit AR-71C). Family Muridae entries verbatim: 'Mus musculus - mice, domesticated'; 'Rattus sp. - rat, domesticated' (genus-level, NOT species-specific).

HAR §4-71-6 - List of Prohibited Animals (Exhibit AR-71P). Order Rodentia includes Cricetidae, Erethizontidae, Hystricidae, Sciuridae but NOT Family Muridae and NO Rattus/Mus - the domesticated rat is not prohibited.

HRS §150A-6.2 - Animal import. Board maintains prohibited/restricted/conditionally-approved lists; conditionally-approved and restricted animals imported only by permit; unlisted animals prohibited until Board review; case-by-case special permits (incl. 90-day short-term).

HAR Chapter 4-71A - Non-Domestic Animal permit conditions (standard & supplemental conditions; import permits 'nontransferable unless otherwise specified in the permit'; post-entry inspection authority).

HDOA - Importing Animals to Hawai'i + Application for Permits (Form PQ-7; conditionally-approved rats/mice/guinea pigs/chinchillas; Honolulu-only entry; Airport Animal Quarantine Holding Facility inspection; CVI).

50 CFR 14.4 - USFWS definition of 'Domesticated animals' (names 'White lab rat - Rattus norvegicus' and 'White lab mouse - Mus musculus'; Rattus rattus NOT listed). Relevant to INTERNATIONAL movement only, not mainland-to-Hawaii.
